layerDoc.newObjectsHelp: Say what goes at each colour. The whole scene goes to Qwen with your marks; each object comes back as its own layer at that place and size, without a shadow (Automatic shadows makes them). Prompt+ sees the marks too.
layerDoc.newObjectsDraw: Draw where a new object goes (an outline or a scribble), one colour per object.
layerDoc.wantPlaceholder: What goes at the {colour} marks, e.g. “a green glass bottle”

layerDoc.multiHelp: Moved and scaled together. Edit together gives Qwen the whole scene; the selected objects take the result's look.
layerDoc.groupTitle: Keep them together: a click on one selects all ({key})
layerDoc.editTogetherTitle: The whole scene as the image to edit; the selected objects take the result's look, the other layers stay
layerDoc.redrawManyTitle: The AI draws each scaled-up object again at the size it has now, sharp (one edit each). Quality and the size menu under the prompt apply
layerDoc.resetPlaceManyTitle: Back to where they were in the photo
layerDoc.deleteManyTitle: Remove them from the layers (with their shadows; the versions stay in the project)
layerDoc.helpBackground: The prompt edits the background. Fill the holes sets up the fill; widen the area with Paint area (shadows too) before Generate.
layerDoc.helpFollows: Moves and scales with its object. Make it again after a big move.
layerDoc.helpBlend: The AI's redrawn scene round the objects (their shadows, reflections, where they touch the ground), on top of them. Something wrong? The Eraser (E) takes it out of this layer. Moved an object? Blend again.
layerDoc.helpEffect: Made where the objects are: make them again after moving objects.
layerDoc.helpObject: The prompt edits this layer at its own size, e.g. “Complete the {name}, keep the transparent background”.
layerDoc.stretchedHelp: Scaled up {scale}×: its pixels are stretched, so it looks soft. Redraw at this size has the AI draw it again at this size, sharp. For more detail pick 1.5K or 2K in the size menu under the prompt first.
layerDoc.fillHolesTitle: Paints the holes as an Add with a prompt to fine-tune, ready to generate
layerDoc.redrawOneTitle: The AI draws this object again at the size it has now, sharp: same shape and colours. Quality and the size menu under the prompt apply. The result replaces the layer at this size (scale back to 100 %); Versions keeps the stretched one
layerDoc.cleanEdgesTitle: Quality: the AI redraws the object's border at its own size, as a cut-out on transparency; the result stays inside its outline (grown ~3 px)
layerDoc.quickCutTitle: Fast: a quick cut-out from the photo, a few seconds (the first time, the sticker model is downloaded: 224 MB)
layerDoc.versionsTitle: Show an earlier version of this layer
layerDoc.resetPlaceTitle: Back to where it was in the photo
layerDoc.deleteTitle: Remove it from the layers (the version stays in the project)
layerDoc.selectHelp: Select a layer (here or on the image) to edit it with the prompt below. Shift+click selects more; the pencil (P) draws new objects.
layerDoc.toolEraser: Eraser (E): erase part of the selected layer (an object or a shadow)
layerDoc.toolShade: Shadow brush (B): paint soft shadow on the selected shadow layer
layerDoc.toolPencil: Pencil (P): draw where a new object goes, one colour per object
layerDoc.toolArea: Area brush (A): change the pink area of the next edit · right-click takes out
layerDoc.blendStaleTitle: Something moved since the blend: its shadows and reflections no longer fit. Blend again (the selected objects, else all)
layerDoc.blendTitle: Experimental: often does not work yet. The AI reads where each object stands (you can correct it), then redraws the scene with their shadows, reflections on wet or shiny ground, grass round their feet; only that is kept, as the Blend layer (the selected objects, else all)
layerDoc.strengthTitle: How strong the blend's shadows and reflections are, without making them again (0 %: none, 100 %: as the model made them, 200 %: twice as strong)
layerDoc.exportPsdTitle: Save the layers as a Photoshop file (.psd), each one a layer, to open in Photoshop, Photopea, GIMP or Krita

lora.title: Your LoRA files (beta)
lora.intro: Load LoRAs made for Qwen-Image 2.1 (.safetensors). Kokon checks each file and keeps its own prepared copy; your file is not changed. Turn them on or off for each project with the LoRA button next to the prompt, up to {max} at a time.
lora.betaNote: Beta: tested on Windows with an NVIDIA card. It should work the same on Mac and Linux, but it hasn't been tested there yet: please tell us how it goes on GitHub.
lora.turboNote: Most LoRAs are trained on the full Qwen-Image 2.1 model, while Kokon runs the faster Turbo model. The popular ones we tested didn't improve on what Turbo does with a good prompt, so compare with the LoRA on and off. A LoRA makes each image about 20 % slower.
aiCheck.sourceCompositeWithTrainedAlgori: made or changed with generative AI
aiCheck.verdictKokon: Made or changed with AI in Kokon
aiCheck.dialogLabel: Check an image for AI marking
aiCheck.title: Check an image
aiCheck.intro: Kokon marks every image it makes or changes with AI twice: in the file's information, and with an invisible watermark that stays when the file is copied, resized or turned into a JPEG. Check any image here. It is read on the computer running Kokon and not kept.
aiCheck.noProof: That does not prove it was not made with AI: markings can be removed, and not every app adds them.
aiCheck.watermarkNotChecked: Not checked: the watermark model is not installed.
aiCheck.watermarkOther: A TrustMark watermark from another app (reads "{text}")
aiCheck.saysNothing: Says nothing about how it was made
aiCheck.markingText: Images Kokon makes or changes say so in their file information and in an invisible watermark, as the EU AI Act asks. Please don't remove them.
advanced.referenceDetailHint: The source images share the GPU budget with the image being drawn. 1 MP leaves more of it for the result, which renders larger and faster; Full gives the model finer source detail but halves the result's size. New chats start at 1 MP.
advanced.keepHdrHint: The HEIC source has an HDR gain map. The result is saved as an Ultra HDR JPEG; the HDR boost fades where the edit changed brightness.
upscalers.superscaleNoteMac: Sharp and natural, but very slow on a Mac: about 6 minutes to enlarge a 1 MP image to 2K on an M2 Pro. On JPEG photos and dark areas it can draw a faint grid.
upscalers.superscaleNote: The default. Sharp and natural on most photos and renders. On JPEG photos and dark areas it can draw a faint grid: lower the strength if you see one.
upscalers.mosrNoteMac: Included with Kokon and the fastest AI upscaler on a Mac (about half a minute per megapixel on an M2 Pro), but on clean images enlarged less than about 3× it draws a fine grid pattern.
upscalers.mosrNote: Included with Kokon and the fastest. Good for big enlargements (4×), but on clean images enlarged less than about 3× it draws a fine grid pattern.
upscalers.ultrasharpNoteMac: Very clean, never a grid. But it smooths skin and textures into an artificial look and can invent lines and shapes, especially at night. Non-commercial license. Very slow on a Mac (minutes per image).
upscalers.ultrasharpNote: Very clean, never a grid. But it smooths skin and textures into an artificial look and can invent lines and shapes, especially at night. Non-commercial license.
upscalers.lanczosNoteMac: The default on a Mac: a plain resize in about a second. It never invents anything, but enlargements look soft.
upscalers.lanczosNote: A plain resize: never invents anything, but enlargements look soft.
upscalers.scenarioFaceHint: A 1.5K render enlarged to 2K. Look at the wrinkles and skin pores.
upscalers.scenarioJpegHint: A JPEG portrait. Look at the forehead: some models turn JPEG blocks into a grid.
upscalers.scenarioNightHint: Wet street with neon lights. Look for lines and squares that aren't in the scene.
upscalers.scenarioTextHint: Gold letters on a shop sign: edges should stay clean.
upscalers.scenarioLandscapeHint: Rocks on a mountain, from a JPEG: fine detail without patterns.
upscalers.scenarioX4Hint: The Upscale button at 4×: every model has to invent detail here.
upscalers.compareIntro: The upscaler enlarges results to their final size and runs the Upscale button. Same crops, enlarged by each one and shown at 2× zoom.
upscalers.notInstalled: Not installed yet: until then MoSR is used.
upscalers.strengthHint: How much of the upscaler's result is kept; the rest is a plain resize. Lower it if it adds texture or patterns that aren't in the image.
upscalers.notSureHint: See them side by side on a face, a JPEG photo, text and a night street.
remote.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices sign in again.

remote.intro: Open Kokon in a browser on your phone, tablet or another computer on the same network. Images are made on this computer and saved in its gallery; each device can download them.
remote.forced: Turned on for this run by kokon-service --remote.
remote.scan: Scan it with your phone's camera
remote.openOnDevice: Or open <url>{url}</url> on the other device. To keep Kokon on the home screen like an app: on iPhone, Share → Add to Home Screen; on Android, the browser's menu → Add to Home screen. The router can give this computer another address later: reserve it in the router's settings (DHCP reservation) so the icon keeps working.
remote.onAtPort: On, at port {port} of this computer's network address.
remote.removePasswordRow: Remove the password and turn access off
remote.goodToKnowText: It works while Kokon is open on this computer. Use it on a network you trust, like your home Wi-Fi: the connection is not encrypted, so avoid public or shared networks. To reach Kokon from outside, use a private network such as Tailscale, never port forwarding on your router. The first time, your system may ask to allow Kokon on the network: allow it on private networks.
remote.videoTitle: A video of setting it up on a phone, on YouTube (opens in your browser)
settings.openSourceText: Code, issues and discussions are on GitHub. A star helps other people find it.
settings.supportText: Kokon is free and made by one person. If it's useful to you, a tip helps keep it that way.
settings.restoreDefaultTitle: Go back to Kokon's built-in instructions

settings.benchPasteHint: Paste the report in the GitHub discussion: it shows which paths suit this chip. Nothing is sent by Kokon.

settings.title: Settings
settings.projectFoldersHint: New images go to a folder named after their project, with the date in the file name, instead of one folder per day. Images already saved stay where they are.
settings.appearanceHint: System follows your computer's light or dark mode. Applies at once.
settings.keepServerRunning: Keep inference server running after closing the app
settings.keepServerRunningHint: Keeps the model loaded so the next start is instant.
settings.idleUnload: Free the graphics card after idle minutes
settings.idleUnloadHint: When nothing is being made for this long, the model leaves the graphics card's memory, even with Kokon open, so other programs can use it. The next image loads it again first. 0 keeps it loaded.
settings.browserVersion: Kokon {version} on the computer running it. It updates there.
settings.updateCheck: Check for updates once a day
settings.updateCheckHint: Only asks GitHub for the latest version number; nothing about you or your images is sent. Updates install when you click them.
settings.welcomeScreen: Welcome screen: what Kokon is and how it keeps your work private
settings.tour: Tour: a short walk through an example project (adds the examples again if you removed them)
settings.promptPlusIntro: With Prompt+ on (next to the prompt), the model's own language model rewrites your prompt before making the image, following these instructions. It always writes in English. Its menu also lets you read and change the prompt before the image is made.
settings.promptPlusNoEngine: The inference engine in use cannot write prompts: Prompt+ appears with an engine that can.
settings.promptPlusWarning: Kokon was tested only with its built-in instructions. Your own can make results worse, or make the model answer with something that is not a prompt; Restore default brings the built-in ones back.
settings.enhancerT2iHelp: Used when creating an image from the prompt alone.
settings.enhancerEditHelp: Used when editing or combining images; the model sees the images.
settings.enhancerComposeHelp: Used for a new image that uses your images as references (New image with images added). Each image is first labelled on its own; these instructions then write the scene from the labels.
settings.modelSetupText: Downloads the official Qwen-Image 2.1 weights for your graphics card, uses model files you already have, or switches between the 12, 16, 24 and 32 GB presets.
settings.officialModelDownloaded: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo, tested with Kokon. Downloaded.
settings.officialModelNotDownloaded: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo, tested with Kokon. Not downloaded into this folder yet: Download… gets it, or use model files you already have.
settings.discardOpenSetup: Discard the unsaved changes and open the model setup?
settings.discardOwnFiles: Discard the unsaved changes and choose your own model files?
settings.ownFilesText: Your own files: not tested by Kokon. Set up models… checks them and finds them again if they move.
settings.imageModelUpdateOfficial: Kokon now uses unsloth's Q4_K_M of the image model: better supported, slightly better, the same 4-bit size. Switching downloads it and deletes the old file from Kokon's folder.
settings.imageModelUpdateOwn: Your image model is the Q4_K file Kokon used before. Kokon now uses unsloth's Q4_K_M: better supported, slightly better, the same 4-bit size. Switching downloads it into Kokon's folder; your own file stays where it is.
settings.saveOrDiscardFirst: Save or discard your changes first
settings.decoderImproved: The new decoder: no fine grid pattern on skin, hair and smooth areas.
settings.decoderUpdateOfficial: A new decoder removes the fine grid pattern on skin, hair and smooth areas, with the same speed and colours. Switching downloads it and deletes the old one from Kokon's folder.
settings.decoderUpdateOwn: A new decoder removes the fine grid pattern on skin, hair and smooth areas, with the same speed and colours. Switching downloads it and deletes the old one from Kokon's folder; your own VAE file stays where it is.
settings.upscalePrescaleHint: Gives the upscaler a smaller image, like the ones it was trained on: fewer invented patterns on clean renders and faster, slightly less fine detail. Only for enlargements under 2.8×.
settings.legacyText: {files}: not the selected model. Only Kokon's own folder is checked.
settings.macEngineHint: Kokon's own engine for Apple Silicon: the GPU, the CPU's matrix unit and the Neural Engine work together, about 4 times faster. New images, edits, brushed edits, extending and Prompt+ work on it; LoRAs and the upscaler model still need it off.
settings.benchNeedsMacEngine: Turn on Kokon's Mac engine and save first
settings.modelMemoryHint: Keep loaded: every model stays in memory, fastest between steps; needs 24 GB or more. Load when needed: each model (text encoder, image model, decoder) is loaded from the SSD when it runs and released after, so the image model has room to work on 16 GB Macs. It adds a few seconds per image. macOS cannot swap memory the GPU is using, so this is what makes 16 GB work.
settings.switchEngineHint: To switch engine, use Models → Set up models…: it downloads the other engine if needed. Both can stay installed.
settings.textEncoderWeightsHint: RAM (recommended): weights in system memory, computed on the GPU. CPU uses the least VRAM but makes image editing several times slower.
settings.sageUnsupported: Needs an RTX 30 series or newer card; off on this one.
settings.vulkanTileHint: With Vulkan, images are decoded in tiles of 512 px at most: larger tiles exceed the driver's buffer limit on AMD cards and get much slower.
settings.prefixCacheHint: Reuses the reference image and prompt across steps so each step only computes the new image. 8-bit (recommended) uses the least memory; FP16 is more exact but needs twice the memory.
settings.prefixCacheHintCuda: Reuses the reference image and prompt across steps so each step only computes the new image. 8-bit (recommended) uses the least memory; FP16 is more exact but needs twice the memory; Auto uses FP32 when SageAttention is on and usually does not fit.
settings.upscaleTileSizeHint: Automatic: 768 px with 16 GB of GPU memory or more (fastest), 256 px below (about 1 GB less).
settings.vramOverrideHint: Plans image sizes as if the card had this much memory (e.g. 12288 to test a 12 GB card). Combine with the VRAM ballast script in scripts/dev so the memory is really unavailable.
settings.serverLocalOnly: The server always listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

tour.exampleText: Kokon made these images on a PC like yours, about half a minute each. This project is yours to look around in, edit further or delete.
tour.versionsText: A sentence made the first image. Painting an area then removed the scooter and added the cat. Click any version to go back to it and continue from there.
tour.compareText: Press and hold the image (or hold B) to see the version it was made from. Slider, Flicker and Changes compare the two in other ways.
tour.describeText: Type what should change in plain words, like “make it a rainy evening”, and press Enter. New image starts from a sentence instead of a picture.
tour.paintText: Paint area: brush over part of the image and only that part changes. Remove, replace, add or change what is there.
tour.projectsText: More examples are here. Start your own with New image, or drop or paste a photo anywhere in the window.
welcome.madeOnText: Your graphics chip creates every image. Photos and prompts never leave this computer.
welcome.onlineText: To download the model, and once a day to check for a new Kokon version. Your images and prompts are never sent.
welcome.noLimitsText: No account, no credits, no subscription, no queue. Create as much as you like.
welcome.privateText: Click the eye icon and nothing is kept: no gallery, no files, no history.
welcome.title: Welcome to Kokon
welcome.lead: A private image studio that lives on your {machine}. Describe a new image, or a change to a photo, in plain words. Like a cocoon, Kokon is a closed space where something new takes shape, and nothing gets out unless you take it out.
welcome.updateCheck: Check for Kokon updates once a day
welcome.openAgain: You can open this again from Settings → General.
welcome.slideDemoText: Create, edit, combine and expand: the whole flow in under a minute.
welcome.slideRemoveText: Paint the scooter · Remove · “the red scooter”
welcome.slideReplaceText: “Replace the yellow armchair with a deep green velvet sofa and hang an abstract painting above it”
welcome.slideRelightText: “Make it a snowy winter night, warm light glowing from the cabin windows”
welcome.slideRestyleText: “Turn it into a hand-painted watercolor illustration”
welcome.slideTextText: “Change the gold sign text to ‘KOKON CAFÉ’”
welcome.slideExpandText: Expand 40 % left and right · “continue the rocky coastline and the turquoise sea”
welcome.showcaseTitle: While you wait: what you can do
welcome.readyDrop: Drop or paste a photo, then describe the change: “make it golden hour”.
welcome.readyNewImage: Switch to New image and describe something that does not exist yet.
welcome.readyPaint: Use Paint area to brush over part of a photo, and only that part changes.
welcome.readyPrivate: Want nothing saved? Turn on Private mode with the eye icon at the top.
promptTips.actionWhy: With a short prompt the model draws the subject and fills the rest with the most ordinary choice.
promptTips.actionNote1: Sitting on a post, with a football.
promptTips.actionPrompt2: Photograph of a monkey dribbling a basketball on an outdoor court, full body, sunny afternoon
promptTips.actionLesson: Who, doing what, where, in what light.
promptTips.negativeWhy: The model reads the words, not the grammar: “no laptop” puts a laptop in its head.
promptTips.negativePrompt1: Photograph of a minimalist wooden desk by a window, no laptop, no computer
promptTips.negativePrompt2: Photograph of a minimalist wooden desk by a window, the desk is clean and empty except for a small potted plant and a ceramic cup
promptTips.negativeLesson: Say what is there. “An empty beach”, not “no people”.
promptTips.textTitle: Text goes in quotes, and short
promptTips.textWhy: Big titles come out right almost every time. Long lines of small text are where it slips.
promptTips.textPrompt1: Minimal concert poster, a white crescent moon, title "NIGHT JAZZ", below it smaller text "Friday 24 October · Teatro Verdi · 21:00"
promptTips.textNote1: The small line appears twice, with a typo.
promptTips.textPrompt2: Minimal concert poster, dark blue background, a large white crescent moon in the center. Only two lines of text: the title "NIGHT JAZZ" in big bold letters at the top, and "24 OCTOBER" in small letters at the bottom. Flat graphic style.
promptTips.textLesson: Lots of small text? Switch Quality to Quality (native 2K).
promptTips.detailsWhy: A short prompt isn't wrong, just generic. Every detail is a choice you make instead of the model.
promptTips.detailsPrompt2: Photograph of a young woman riding a vintage blue bicycle along a seaside promenade, her hair blowing in the wind, a basket of flowers on the handlebar, late afternoon golden light, shot from the side, full body
promptTips.detailsLesson: Long prompts are fine. Plain sentences, most important things first.
promptTips.betterWhy: Ask to “improve” a photo and you get it back almost unchanged.
promptTips.betterPrompt2: Make the room cozy for a winter evening: dusk outside the window, the floor lamp turned on with warm light, a knitted cream blanket on the armchair, a stack of books and a mug of tea on the rug
promptTips.betterLesson: Turn “better” into things you can see: warmer light, tidier, a sunset.
promptTips.nameTitle: Name the thing you want changed
promptTips.nameWhy: Without a name, the model picks the most eye-catching thing in the photo.
promptTips.namePrompt2: Paint the wall behind the armchair a dusty blue. Keep the yellow armchair and everything else unchanged.

whatsNew.v0_12_1_moreLikeThisText: Under a new image, More like this makes another one from it: Subtle keeps the picture and changes the details, Strong keeps the idea and changes more. Regenerate still starts from scratch.
whatsNew.v0_12_1_redrawText: In the Layers lab, an object made bigger with the corner handle can be drawn again at its new size, so it stays sharp. The stretched version stays under Versions.
whatsNew.v0_12_1_gpuFreedTitle: The GPU is freed when Kokon is idle
whatsNew.v0_12_1_gpuFreedText: After 10 idle minutes the model leaves the GPU even with a Kokon window or browser tab open, so other programs can use it. It loads again with the next image.
whatsNew.v0_12_1_projectFolderText: Settings → General → A folder for each project: new images are saved in a folder named after their project instead of one folder per day. Off unless you turn it on.
whatsNew.v0_12_1_fixesText: The time saved in an image's file is local time (it was an hour early in Europe), and when Kokon cannot start its service it says why, for example a processor without AVX.
whatsNew.heading: What's new in Kokon {version}
whatsNew.includeModel: Include the new image model file
whatsNew.modelBodyOwn: Your image model is the Q4_K file Kokon used before. Kokon now uses unsloth's Q4_K_M: better supported, slightly better, the same 4-bit size. Kokon can download it into its own folder and use it; your file stays where it is, untouched. You can also switch later in Settings → Models.
whatsNew.modelBody: Kokon now uses unsloth's Q4_K_M of Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo: better supported, slightly better, the same 4-bit size. The old file is deleted once the new one is downloaded and checked. You can also switch later in Settings → Models.
whatsNew.modelWhyText: Both are 4-bit copies of Qwen's Turbo model and look much the same. The Q4_K_M comes from unsloth, one of the most used sources of GGUF models, and it is the file Kokon's tests and its Mac engine are checked against. Same license as the model.
whatsNew.vaeBody: For the cleaner images above, Kokon needs to replace the decoder it installed. The old file is deleted once the new one is in place. If you keep the current one, you can switch any time in Settings → Models.
whatsNew.vaeBodyOwn: For the cleaner images above, Kokon needs to replace the decoder it installed. The old file is deleted once the new one is in place. Your own VAE file stays where it is: Kokon uses its own copy. If you keep the current one, you can switch any time in Settings → Models.
whatsNew.vaeWhatText: The decoder (VAE, variational autoencoder) turns the model's result into pixels. Qwen's original decoder leaves a faint 2-pixel checkerboard on fine texture. This version, retrained by madebyollin (the author of TAESD), removes it: the image, its colours and the time stay the same. Same license as the model.
whatsNew.engineBody: A newer stable-diffusion.cpp is ready, the engine that runs the models on your graphics chip. Your images, models and settings stay as they are.
whatsNew.engineBodySuperscale: A newer stable-diffusion.cpp is ready, the engine that runs the models on your graphics chip, plus the Superscale-SP model. Your images, models and settings stay as they are.
whatsNew.failedHint: Try again, or open Settings → Models to do it later.

setup.engineNoteCuda: NVIDIA's CUDA build: the fastest and tested path. Recommended.
setup.engineNoteMetal: Beta. Runs on the Mac's GPU through Metal. Needs macOS 15 or newer.
setup.engineNoteVulkanNvidia: The same model through Vulkan: works on NVIDIA, but slower than CUDA (no SageAttention) and the first image takes longer. Useful to try the AMD / Intel path; both engines can stay installed.
setup.engineNoteVulkan: Beta. AMD and Intel cards run the model through Vulkan, with the graphics driver you already have. Not yet tested on a real AMD or Intel card: please report how it goes.

setup.leadOwn: Everything runs on this PC. Use the Qwen-Image 2.1 files you already have, for example from ComfyUI: Setup only downloads the engine and what you don't have.
setup.leadOfficial: Everything runs on this PC. Setup downloads the image model once ({size}); after that, nothing leaves your computer.
setup.leadOfficialAbout: Everything runs on this PC. Setup downloads the image model once (about 12 GB); after that, nothing leaves your computer.
setup.promptPlusEngine: This version of Kokon brings Prompt+, which needs Kokon's updated engine: press Install to download it ({size}). Until then, everything else works as before and Prompt+ stays hidden.
setup.noGpuNote: Kokon needs a graphics card with at least 12 GB of VRAM: NVIDIA (RTX 20 series or newer), or AMD / Intel through Vulkan (beta), or a Mac with Apple Silicon. Make sure its driver is installed.
setup.unifiedSlowNote: With {memory} of unified memory Kokon works, but slowly: model weights are read from disk as needed and images are made at about 1 megapixel, which takes about 4 to 5 minutes on an M2 Pro. 32 GB or more and a Pro, Max or Ultra chip are recommended. Close other apps while generating.
setup.unifiedMinutesNote: With {memory} of unified memory expect several minutes per image. 32 GB or more and a Pro, Max or Ultra chip are recommended.
setup.lowVramNote: Your GPU has {vram} of VRAM. 8 GB is the smallest size Kokon runs on (in beta); it may fail or run slowly.
setup.vram8gbNote: 8 GB graphics cards are in beta: images are made at about 1 megapixel, and an edit takes 1–2 minutes on an RTX 5050 Laptop. Tell us how it runs on yours.
setup.lowRamNote: The text encoder runs from system RAM; with {ram} of RAM, 16 GB or more is recommended.
setup.useOwnModelsDetail: From ComfyUI or another folder; only the engine is downloaded
setup.oneCardNote: Kokon runs on one card. The preset is sized for the card you pick; you can change it later in Settings → Performance.
setup.presetOwnNote: How Kokon runs the model on your card: memory use and image sizes. Your files are kept.
setup.notTestedMac: Not yet tested on a Mac.
setup.betaUserTested: Beta: tested by users, not yet by us.
setup.notTestedCardSize: Not yet tested on a real card of this size.
setup.macPresetNote: Presets are named by total unified memory. macOS lets the graphics part use about two thirds of it, and the text encoder shares the same memory, so the image model gets less than the number on your Mac: a 16 GB Mac has room for the lightest preset only. Pick a larger one only on a Mac with that much memory.
setup.notEnoughSpace: not enough space on this drive; choose another folder.
setup.resumeNote: Downloads continue where they stopped, also after closing the app.

setup.licenseFoot: Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo is released by Alibaba's Qwen team under the Qwen Research License: research and evaluation only, no commercial use. By downloading it you accept that license. The upscalers are Superscale-SP by Nmkd (WTFPL) and the experimental 4xNomos2_hq_mosr by Philip Hofmann (CC BY 4.0). Downloads come only from GitHub (stable-diffusion.cpp, upscaler) and Hugging Face, and every file is verified with its SHA-256 checksum.

blendChoice.title: Blend into the scene
blendChoice.lead_one: The AI looked at where the object stands. It redraws the scene with what that place does: the contact shadow, the shadow, a reflection on wet or shiny ground. Check what it read and change anything that is wrong. It is experimental and often does not work yet: blending all the objects at once works best.
